capabilities: Sync notes and attachments across devices through a self-hosted server
Browse, compare and restore note versions and deleted notes
Restore a folder or the whole vault to a chosen date and time
Serve notes to AI agents through a built-in MCP endpoint
Sync Obsidian settings, themes, snippets and plugin settings
extras: Free and open source under MIT. No end-to-end encryption: the server stores notes, versions and filenames in plaintext, which is what allows the MCP endpoint to work. Windows is not supported and iOS is untested; files are limited to 64 MiB by default and plugins and hidden files do not sync.
intentEvidence: TrewSync is a fork of Basalt Sync, made by its own author, Wayne Hoover
problem: Users who want their vault synced through a server they run themselves, with full version history and agent access to the same notes, have no single tool that provides all three.

relations.evidence: TrewSync is a fork of Basalt Sync, made by its own author, Wayne Hoover
Pick TrewSync for history on your own server and agents on the same notes.
Runs on | Your server | Obsidian's servers | Your backend, such as CouchDB or S3-compatible storage
An agent such as Claude Code searches, reads and edits the same notes your devices sync
You need a Linux or macOS machine with Docker, and Tailscale on it and on each device.

summary: Self-hosted sync server and Obsidian plugin that keeps every note version and lets AI agents read and edit the same notes over MCP.
